translations.1: Then God said to Moses: 'Go in to Pharaoh, and say to him: Thus says God, the God of the Hebrews — release my people that they may serve me.
translations.2: For if you refuse to release them, and you persist in holding them,
translations.3: then a plague of God shall come upon your livestock which are in the open country — upon the horses and the donkeys and the camels, and the cattle and the flock — a very great pestilence.
translations.4: And God shall distinguish between the livestock of the sons of Israel and the livestock of the Egyptians, and not a single thing of all that belongs to the sons of Israel shall die.'
translations.5: And God appointed a time, saying: 'Tomorrow God shall do this thing in the land.'
translations.6: And God did this thing on the morrow; and all the livestock of the Egyptians died, and of the livestock of the sons of Israel not one died.
translations.7: And Pharaoh sent and looked — and behold, not one of the livestock of the sons of Israel had died. And his heart was hardened, and he did not release the people.
translations.8: And God said to Moses and Aaron: 'Take for yourselves your double-handful of soot from the furnace, and Moses shall scatter it into the air in the presence of Pharaoh;
translations.9: and it shall become dust over all the land of Egypt, and it shall be upon the people and upon the beasts — a boil breaking out in blisters — over all the land of Egypt.'
translations.10: So they took from the soot of the furnace, and stood before Pharaoh; and Moses scattered it into the air, and there came boils breaking out in blisters, growing upon the people and upon the beasts.
translations.11: And the learned men were unable to stand before Moses on account of the boil, for it was upon them and upon the rest of the Egyptians.
translations.12: And God hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he did not accept from them — as God had said to Moses.
translations.13: And God said to Moses: 'Rise early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh, and say to him: Thus says God, the God of the Hebrews — release my people that they may serve me.
translations.14: For in this instance I am sending many of my plagues into your heart, and against your officers and your people — so that you may know that there is none like me in all the world.
translations.15: For now, had I unleashed my plagues, I would have struck you and your people with pestilence, and you would have been obliterated from the land.
translations.16: But it is for this very reason that I have kept you alive — to show you my power, and so that my name may be told throughout all the world.
translations.17: Yet you are still bent upon my people, so as not to release them.
translations.18: Behold, I am about to rain down at about this same time tomorrow a very great hail, the like of which has not been in Egypt from the day it was founded until now.
translations.19: So send now — secure your livestock and all that you have in the open country; for any person or beast found in the open country that does not take shelter in the dwellings — the hail shall fall upon them and they shall die.'
translations.20: Whoever among Pharaoh's officers feared the word of God drove his servants and his livestock into the houses.
translations.21: And whoever did not turn his heart to the word of God left his servants and his livestock in the open country.
translations.22: And God said to Moses: 'Stretch out your hand toward the sky, that there be hail over all the land of Egypt — upon the people and upon the beasts, and upon all the grass of the open country in the land of Egypt.'
translations.23: And Moses stretched out his staff toward the sky; and God proclaimed thunderclaps and hail, and fire moved along the earth; and God rained down hail upon the land of Egypt.
translations.24: And there was hail, with fire blazing in its midst — very great, the like of which had not been in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation.
translations.25: And the hail struck throughout all the land of Egypt everything that was in the open country, from person to beast; and the hail struck all the grass thereof, and shattered all the trees thereof.
translations.26: Except in the land of Goshen, where the sons of Israel were — there was no hail.
translations.27: And Pharaoh sent and called for Moses and Aaron, and said to them: 'I have sinned this time — God is the just one, and I and my people are the wrongdoers.
translations.28: Intercede with God; for it is enough that there have been thunderclaps of God and hail upon us — and I shall release you, and you need not remain any longer.'
translations.29: Then Moses said: 'When I go out from the town, I shall spread out my hands to God, and the thunderclaps shall cease, and the hail shall be no more — so that you may know that the earth belongs to God.
translations.30: But as for you and your officers, I know that you have yet to fear the presence of God.'
translations.31: Now the flax and the barley had been ruined, for the barley was already in ear and the flax was in bud.
translations.32: But the wheat and the spelt were not ruined, for they are late-growing.
translations.33: And when Moses went out from Pharaoh and from his town, he spread out his hands to God; and the thunderclaps and the hail ceased, and no rain poured down upon the earth.
translations.34: And when Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunderclaps had ceased, he went back to sinning — and he and his officers hardened their hearts.
translations.35: And the heart of Pharaoh was hardened, and he did not release them — as God had said to Moses.
